examInfo.title: JAMB Government Practice Questions
examInfo.subject: Government
examInfo.instructions: Choose the correct option from A-D for each question.

questions.question: The concept of separation of powers was first propounded by
questions.explanation: Baron de Montesquieu in his book 'The Spirit of Laws' (1748) first articulated the theory of separation of powers into executive, legislative, and judicial branches.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of federalism?

options.A: Division of powers between central and regional governments

questions.explanation: A unitary system concentrates power in the central government, which is opposite to federalism that divides power between levels of government.

questions.question: The Nigerian constitution that introduced the presidential system of government was the
questions.explanation: The 1979 Constitution introduced the presidential system in Nigeria, replacing the parliamentary system used in the First Republic.

questions.question: Universal adult suffrage means

options.B: All adults regardless of sex, race, or property can vote

questions.explanation: Universal adult suffrage grants voting rights to all adult citizens regardless of gender, race, religion, or economic status.

questions.question: The United Nations Organization was established in
questions.explanation: The United Nations was officially established on October 24, 1945, when the UN Charter came into force.

questions.question: Which organ of government is responsible for law-making?
questions.explanation: The legislature is the law-making organ of government, responsible for enacting, amending, and repealing laws.

questions.question: The principle of rule of law was popularized by
questions.explanation: A.V. Dicey, a British constitutional lawyer, popularized the concept of rule of law in his work 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution' (1885).

questions.question: In a parliamentary system, the head of government is the
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary system, the Prime Minister is the head of government and leads the executive branch.

questions.question: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) was established in
questions.explanation: ECOWAS was established on May 28, 1975, by the Treaty of Lagos to promote economic integration among West African countries.

questions.question: Which of the following is a merit of the multi-party system?

options.B: It is less expensive to operate

questions.explanation: The multi-party system allows different parties to present alternative policies and programs, giving voters choices.

questions.question: The process of removing a president from office is called
questions.explanation: Impeachment is the constitutional process of removing a president or other high officials from office for misconduct.

questions.question: The African Union (AU) replaced the
questions.explanation: The African Union was established in 2001 to replace the Organization of African Unity, which had been founded in 1963.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of political parties?
questions.explanation: Interpretation of laws is a function of the judiciary, not political parties. Political parties focus on political education, leadership recruitment, and interest aggregation.

questions.question: The concept of sovereignty was first developed by
questions.explanation: Jean Bodin, a French political philosopher, first developed the modern concept of sovereignty in his work 'Six Books of the Commonwealth' (1576).

questions.question: In Nigeria, the body responsible for conducting elections is
questions.explanation: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is the constitutional body responsible for conducting elections in Nigeria.

questions.question: The theory that government exists by the consent of the governed was propounded by
questions.explanation: John Locke in his 'Two Treatises of Government' argued that legitimate government exists only with the consent of the governed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of a confederation?
questions.explanation: In a confederation, the central government is weak while the component states retain most of their sovereignty and powers.

questions.question: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in
questions.explanation: The United Nations headquarters is located in New York City, USA, on the East River in Manhattan.

questions.question: The principle of checks and balances ensures that

options.A: One organ of government dominates others
options.B: All organs of government are equal
options.C: No organ of government becomes too powerful

questions.explanation: Checks and balances prevent any single organ of government from becoming too powerful by allowing each organ to limit the powers of others.

questions.question: Which of the following countries practices a unitary system of government?
questions.explanation: Ghana practices a unitary system where power is concentrated in the central government, unlike federal systems in Nigeria, USA, and Canada.

questions.question: The process by which people acquire political attitudes and beliefs is called
questions.explanation: Political socialization is the process through which individuals acquire their political attitudes, beliefs, and values from family, school, media, and society.

questions.question: The first military coup in Nigeria took place in
questions.explanation: The first military coup in Nigeria occurred on January 15, 1966, led by Major Chukwuma Kaduna Nzeogwu and other young officers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a source of the Nigerian constitution?
questions.explanation: While customary law influences Nigerian law, it is not a direct source of the constitution. The constitution draws from colonial constitutions, independence constitution, and military decrees.

questions.question: The International Court of Justice is located in
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the UN, is located in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes democracy?
questions.explanation: Democracy is defined as government by the people, where citizens participate directly or through elected representatives in decision-making.
